feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence: iteration 0 (4 cm span, 12 mm sensors, y 0.05, mass 0.8) lost the line 1.0 to 2.0 times per run. Iteration 1 (plus or minus 3 cm span, 16 mm, y 0.04, mass 0.7) lost it 1.0 per run on every track. Iteration 2 (y 0.03) also stayed at 1.0. Iteration 3 (mass 0.6) also stayed at 1.0, and its score fell from 47.85 to 46.16, so lighter mass alone did not help. Steering oscillation stayed between 0.07 and 0.14 throughout, so the robot is not jittering. Sensing and mass have now each been varied without removing the single bend loss, which points to turn authority or a fixed start-point failure. Decision rules for the next race: (1) If line_loss_events fall to 0.5 or less on the s-bend and slalom with max_error under 0.06 m, keep wheel_radius 0.035 and test wheel_track next (0.16 m) to see if more turn authority helps further. (2) If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 with the larger radius, the response is overshooting: return wheel_radius to 0.03 and keep mass at 0.6 kg. (3) If line_loss_events stay at 1.0 per run with the larger radius, the wheel is not the limit; the next step is to look at where in the course the line is lost (start or a fixed bend) rather than at geometry.
requested_changes: Set wheel_radius to 0.035 m with mass 0.6 kg, wheel_track 0.14 m and sensors at y 0.03 m with the plus or minus 3 cm span. Basis: iterations 0 to 3 showed that sensor span, forward offset and mass each leave line loss at about 1.0 per run, so turn authority is the untested lever.

If line loss falls but still exceeds 0.5 per run, try wheel_track 0.16 m with wheel_radius 0.035 m. Basis: iteration 3 showed that mass reduction alone did not reduce line loss, and wheel_track sets the yaw rate per unit wheel-speed difference, so a wider track is the next turn-authority step.

If steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.2 at radius 0.035 m, return wheel_radius to 0.03 m and keep mass at 0.6 kg. Basis: oscillation was 0.07 to 0.14 across iterations 0 to 3, so there is room before jitter becomes a problem, but a larger radius raises ground speed and could cause overshoot.
